name: Chicago
note: Parameters for chicago.html, in real coordinates: every position is [lat, lon] and is projected to metres around State & Madison (x east, z south). Streets: [name, lon or lat, width m, major 0/1, optional range from, to (lat for north-south streets, lon for east-west)]. Positions are from maps at street-block accuracy; heights are the buildings' real heights. 'bounds' is the map rectangle [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]; addresses were converted with Chicago's grid (800 per mile from State & Madison).

fill._: outside the named streets the grid is filled at Chicago's pitch: north-south streets every 1/16 mile, east-west every 1/8 mile

_shore: the lake shore from north to south; the lake is everything east of it. The bulge at 41.866 is the Adler Planetarium peninsula; Northerly Island continues south.

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]; the first box that contains a block wins

landmarks.name: Willis Tower
landmarks.info: 233 S Wacker Dr · 1974 · 442 m, 108 floors. Nine bundled tubes, stepping back at floors 50, 66 and 90.

landmarks.name: 875 North Michigan
landmarks.info: The John Hancock Center · 1969 · 344 m (457 m to the antennas). A tapered tube with X-bracing on the outside.

landmarks.name: Trump International Hotel & Tower
landmarks.info: 401 N Wabash Ave · 2009 · 357 m to the roof, 423 m with the spire. Three setbacks answer the heights of its neighbours.

landmarks.name: Aon Center
landmarks.info: 200 E Randolph St · 1973 · 346 m. A plain white shaft, once clad in marble.

landmarks.name: St. Regis Chicago
landmarks.info: 363 E Wacker Dr · 2020 · 363 m. Three stems of stacked frusta, the tallest building in the world designed by a woman (Jeanne Gang).

landmarks.name: Aqua
landmarks.info: 225 N Columbus Dr · 2009 · 262 m. Balconies of different depths make the facade ripple like water (Jeanne Gang).

landmarks.name: Two Prudential Plaza
landmarks.info: 180 N Stetson Ave · 1990 · 303 m. Chevron setbacks and a spire.

landmarks.name: Marina City
landmarks.info: 300 N State St · 1964 · 179 m. Two 'corn cob' towers: nineteen floors of spiral parking, then apartments with petal balconies.

landmarks.name: Merchandise Mart
landmarks.info: 222 Merchandise Mart Plaza · 1930 · 100 m. Four million square feet, once the largest building in the world.

landmarks.name: Chicago Board of Trade
landmarks.info: 141 W Jackson Blvd · 1930 · 184 m. Art Deco, closing the view down LaSalle Street; Ceres stands on top.

landmarks.name: 311 South Wacker
landmarks.info: 311 S Wacker Dr · 1990 · 293 m. The lit glass crown is 32 m tall.

landmarks.name: Tribune Tower
landmarks.info: 435 N Michigan Ave · 1925 · 141 m. Neo-Gothic; stones from famous buildings are set into its base.

landmarks.name: Wrigley Building
landmarks.info: 400 N Michigan Ave · 1924 · 130 m. White terra cotta, floodlit at night.

landmarks.name: Crain Communications Building
landmarks.info: 150 N Michigan Ave · 1984 · 177 m. The diamond-shaped top faces the park.

landmarks.name: Lake Point Tower
landmarks.info: 505 N Lake Shore Dr · 1968 · 197 m. Three curved wings of bronze glass, the only skyscraper east of Lake Shore Drive.

landmarks.name: Water Tower
landmarks.info: 806 N Michigan Ave · 1869 · 47 m. Limestone; one of the few buildings to survive the Great Fire of 1871.

landmarks.name: Cloud Gate
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2006 · 'The Bean'. 168 welded stainless-steel plates, 100 tonnes, 20 m long. Walk under the arch at its centre.

landmarks.name: Jay Pritzker Pavilion
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2004 · Frank Gehry. Stainless-steel ribbons over the stage and a lattice of pipes over the lawn.

landmarks.name: Crown Fountain
landmarks.info: Millennium Park · 2004 · Jaume Plensa. Two glass-brick towers showing the faces of Chicagoans; water spouts from their mouths in summer.

landmarks.name: Buckingham Fountain
landmarks.info: Grant Park · 1927. One of the largest fountains in the world; the centre jet reaches 46 m on the hour.

landmarks.name: Art Institute of Chicago
landmarks.info: 111 S Michigan Ave · 1893. Beaux-Arts; the bronze lions guard the steps.

landmarks.name: Union Station
landmarks.info: 225 S Canal St · 1925. The Great Hall's skylight is 35 m up.

landmarks.name: Field Museum
landmarks.info: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr · 1921. Greek-revival marble; Sue the T. rex lives inside.

landmarks.name: Shedd Aquarium
landmarks.info: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr · 1930. An octagonal Beaux-Arts hall on the lake.

landmarks.name: Adler Planetarium
landmarks.info: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr · 1930. America's first planetarium, a twelve-sided Art Deco hall on the peninsula.

landmarks.name: Soldier Field
landmarks.info: 1410 Museum Campus Dr · 1924, rebuilt 2003. The colonnades survive; the bowl inside does not match them.

landmarks.name: Navy Pier
landmarks.info: 600 E Grand Ave · 1916. A kilometre into the lake; the Centennial Wheel is 60 m tall.

landmarks.name: Northwest Tower
landmarks.info: 1600 N Milwaukee Ave · 1929 · 12 storeys. Wicker Park's Art Deco tower at the six-way corner of North, Damen and Milwaukee; now The Robey hotel.

landmarks.name: Flat Iron Building
landmarks.info: 1579 N Milwaukee Ave · 1913 · a three-storey wedge where Milwaukee Avenue meets North Avenue, long full of artists' studios.

landmarks.name: Wicker Park Fountain
landmarks.info: Wicker Park · the park Charles and Joel Wicker gave the city in 1870; the cast-iron fountain is a 2002 recreation of the original.

landmarks.name: Wicker Park Fieldhouse
landmarks.info: 1425 N Damen Ave · Chicago Park District fieldhouse in the triangle between Damen, Schiller and Wicker Park Avenue.

landmarks.name: Pulaski Park Fieldhouse
landmarks.info: 1419 W Blackhawk St · 1914 · William Carbys Zimmermann. Arts and Crafts brick with a tiled roof: gymnasium, auditorium and a theatre, built for the Polish Downtown.

landmarks.name: Pulaski Park Pool
landmarks.info: Pulaski Park · the outdoor pool, open in summer.

landmarks.name: St. Stanislaus Kostka
landmarks.info: 1351 W Evergreen Ave · 1881 · Chicago's first Polish parish, once the largest parish in the United States. The twin towers face Noble Street.

landmarks.name: Holy Trinity Polish Mission
landmarks.info: 1118 N Noble St · 1906 · a Polish Baroque basilica with twin towers, a short walk from Pulaski Park.

landmarks.name: St. Mary of the Angels
landmarks.info: 1850 N Hermitage Ave · 1920 · a Roman Renaissance church with a copper dome modelled on St Peter's, rising over Bucktown.

el._: the Loop elevated: Lake St, Wabash Ave, Van Buren St and Wells St, 8 m up; trains run both ways

blue._: the Blue Line comes up from the Milwaukee subway south of Division and runs elevated past Damen to the northwest

focus.name: North & Ashland
focus._: commercial corners: taller shopfronts, street lights, signals, bus stops, parked cars and people

trails.name: The 606 (Bloomingdale Trail)
trails.info: Bloomingdale Trail · 2015 · a disused rail embankment 5 m above the street, now a 4.4 km park and trail.
